title: System 8: Economy/Shop System
description:
NPC shops with dynamic pricing and faction discounts.

## File Structure
```
lib/exmud/framework/economy/
├── shop.ex               # Shop component behavior
└── pricing.ex            # Dynamic pricing logic
```

## Shop Configuration (YAML - NPC Component)
```yaml
# In NPC prototype
components:
  merchant:
    shop_type: general       # general | weapons | armor | magic
    buy_multiplier: 0.5      # Pays 50% of base price
    sell_multiplier: 1.0     # Sells at 100% of base price
    stock:
      - item: health_potion
        quantity: 10
        restock_time: 3600   # Seconds
      - item: rope
        quantity: 5
        unlimited: true      # Never runs out
    currency: gold           # What currency accepted
    faction_discounts: true  # Apply faction reputation
    greeting: "Welcome to my shop!"
    farewell: "Come again!"
```

## Global Economy Config (YAML)
```yaml
# config/economy.yml
economy:
  supply_demand: true        # Prices change based on quantity
  scarcity_multiplier: 1.5   # Low stock = higher price
  abundance_multiplier: 0.8  # High stock = lower price
  event_effects:
    war: { weapons: 1.5, food: 1.3 }
    festival: { alcohol: 1.2, decorations: 1.3 }
```

## Item Base Price (in item prototype)
```yaml
# In item prototype
components:
  valuable:
    base_price: 50           # Base gold value
    category: consumable     # For event effects
```

## Core Structs
```elixir
defmodule ExMUD.Framework.Economy.ShopItem do
  defstruct [
    :item_key,
    :quantity,           # Current stock (-1 for unlimited)
    :max_quantity,       # Max stock for restock
    :restock_time,       # Seconds between restocks
    :restock_timer       # Runtime: time until next restock
  ]
end

defmodule ExMUD.Framework.Economy.Transaction do
  defstruct [
    :type,               # :buy | :sell
    :item_key,
    :quantity,
    :unit_price,
    :total_price,
    :buyer_id,
    :seller_id,
    :timestamp
  ]
end
```

## API Functions
- `Shop.list_stock(npc)` - Get available items with prices
- `Shop.get_buy_price(npc, item, quantity)` - Price to buy from shop
- `Shop.get_sell_price(npc, item, quantity)` - Price shop pays
- `Shop.buy(entity, npc, item, quantity)` - Purchase from shop
- `Shop.sell(entity, npc, item, quantity)` - Sell to shop
- `Pricing.apply_faction_discount(price, entity, npc)` - Apply reputation
- `Pricing.apply_supply_demand(price, stock, max_stock)` - Dynamic pricing

## Integration Points
- Inventory system for item transfer
- Faction system for reputation discounts
- Events system for economy modifiers (war, festival)
- Day/Night affects shop availability
close_reason: Implemented economy/shop system with shop.ex and economy.ex - buy/sell mechanics, pricing, stock management

title: System 19: Clothing/Appearance System
description:
Worn items affect character description and appearance (inspired by Evennia contribs).

## File Structure
```
lib/exmud/framework/appearance/
├── clothing.ex           # Clothing component and slots
└── appearance.ex         # Character description builder
```

## Clothing Definition (YAML)
```yaml
# priv/world/items/silk_robe.yml
key: silk_robe
name: "Silk Robe"
type: clothing
components:
  wearable:
    slot: body               # body | head | hands | feet | cloak | etc.
    layer: 2                 # Lower = closer to skin
    covers: [torso, arms]    # Body parts covered
    appearance:
      default: "wearing a flowing silk robe"
      wet: "wearing a sodden silk robe"
      damaged: "wearing a tattered silk robe"
  physical:
    weight: 1
    warmth: 2                # Protection from cold
    waterproof: false
description: "A beautiful robe of fine silk."
```

## Clothing Slots & Layers
```yaml
# config/clothing.yml
clothing:
  slots:
    head: [hat, helmet, hood]
    body: [shirt, robe, armor]
    legs: [pants, skirt]
    feet: [boots, sandals]
    hands: [gloves, gauntlets]
    cloak: [cape, cloak]
    neck: [necklace, scarf]
    waist: [belt, sash]
  
  layers:
    # Lower number = closer to skin
    1: undergarments
    2: main_clothing
    3: outer_clothing
    4: armor
    5: cloaks_capes

  # How many items per slot per layer
  max_per_layer: 1
```

## Body Parts
```yaml
body_parts:
  - head
  - face
  - neck
  - torso
  - arms
  - hands
  - waist
  - legs
  - feet
```

## Appearance Building
When looking at a character, clothing described in layer order:
```
You see Tenzin, a wise old monk.
He is wearing a saffron prayer shawl over simple cotton robes.
Around his waist hangs a leather belt with a small pouch.
On his feet are worn leather sandals.
```

## Character Description (YAML)
```yaml
# Player character appearance
components:
  appearance:
    base_description: "a weathered traveler"
    features:
      hair: "long black hair"
      eyes: "piercing grey eyes"
      build: "lean and wiry"
    current_state: null      # wounded | dirty | radiant | etc.
```

## Core Structs
```elixir
defmodule ExMUD.Framework.Appearance.Clothing do
  defstruct [
    :slot,
    :layer,
    :covers,             # [body_part]
    :appearance,         # %{condition => text}
    :warmth,
    :waterproof,
    :condition           # :pristine | :worn | :damaged | :wet
  ]
end

defmodule ExMUD.Framework.Appearance.CharacterAppearance do
  defstruct [
    :base_description,
    :features,           # %{feature => text}
    :current_state,
    :worn_items          # [{slot, layer, entity_id}]
  ]
end
```

## API Functions
- `Clothing.can_wear?(entity, item)` - Check slot/layer available
- `Clothing.wear(entity, item)` - Equip clothing
- `Clothing.remove(entity, slot)` - Remove from slot
- `Clothing.get_worn(entity)` - All worn items
- `Clothing.get_warmth(entity)` - Total warmth value
- `Appearance.build_description(entity)` - Full character description
- `Appearance.get_clothing_description(entity)` - Just clothing text

## Integration Points
- Look command shows appearance
- Weather affects clothing condition (wet)
- Combat can damage clothing
- Warmth protects from cold weather
- Social interactions may react to appearance

title: System 13: Companion/Pet System
description:
NPCs or creatures that follow players, assist in combat, and require care.

## File Structure
```
lib/exmud/framework/companions/
├── companion.ex          # Companion definition and loading
├── companion_manager.ex  # Follow/command/care logic
└── companion_ai.ex       # Combat assistance behavior
```

## Companion Definition (YAML)
```yaml
# priv/world/companions/wolf.yml
key: wolf_companion
name: "Wolf"
type: combat                 # combat | utility | passive
base_stats:
  health: 50
  attack: 8
  defense: 4
abilities:
  - bite                     # Reference to ability system
  - howl
commands:                    # Player commands
  - attack                   # Attack current target
  - defend                   # Protect player
  - follow                   # Default follow mode
  - stay                     # Wait in current room
  - dismiss                  # Send companion away
loyalty:
  starting: 0                # Starts at 0, grows with care
  max: 100
  decay_rate: 5              # Per day without interaction
loyalty_effects:
  - min: 50
    bonus: [attack_assist]   # Assists in combat
  - min: 75
    bonus: [warning]         # Alerts to hidden enemies
  - min: 100
    bonus: [damage_share]    # Takes 20% of player damage
upkeep:
  food_per_day: 2            # Needs feeding
  food_types: [meat, fish]   # What it eats
tame_difficulty: 3           # Skill check difficulty
tame_skill: animal_handling
description: "A loyal grey wolf."
```

## Companion Types
- **Combat**: Assists in battle (wolf, bear, hawk)
- **Utility**: Provides bonuses (pack mule, hunting dog)
- **Passive**: Cosmetic or minimal bonus (cat, bird)

## Companion Sources
- **Taming**: Wild creatures (requires skill)
- **Purchase**: From vendors
- **Quest reward**: Special companions
- **Summoning**: Via abilities (temporary)

## Player Companion State

  companion_slot:
    active_companion: wolf_companion_instance_123
    max_companions: 1        # How many can have
```

## Companion Instance (spawned entity)
```yaml

key: wolf_companion_instance_123
prototype: wolf_companion
components:
  companion:
    owner_id: player_123
    name: "Fenrir"           # Player-given name
    loyalty: 75
    last_fed: ~U[2024-01-20 12:00:00Z]
    current_command: follow
```

## Core Structs
```elixir
defmodule ExMUD.Framework.Companions.Companion do
  defstruct [
    :key,
    :name,
    :type,
    :base_stats,
    :abilities,
    :commands,
    :loyalty,
    :upkeep,
    :tame_difficulty,
    :tame_skill,
    :description

defmodule ExMUD.Framework.Companions.CompanionInstance do

    :owner_id,

    :loyalty,

    :current_health

```

- `Companion.summon(entity, companion_key)` - Summon via ability
- `Companion.dismiss(entity)` - Remove active companion
- `Companion.command(entity, command)` - Issue command

- `Companion.rename(entity, new_name)` - Change name
- `Companion.get_active(entity)` - Get active companion
- `CompanionAI.combat_action(companion, combat_state)` - Auto action

- Combat system for assistance

title: Implement event circular buffer in GameLive
description:
Memory leak: Event list in GameLive grows unbounded.

File: lib/exmud_web/live/game_live.ex

Pattern:
```elixir
|> update(:events, fn events -> events ++ [event] end)
```

Impact: With 1000 players × 100 events = 100KB × 1000 = 100MB+ of RAM

Fix: Implement circular buffer limiting to last 50-100 events:
```elixir
|> update(:events, fn events -> 
  Enum.take(events ++ [event], -50)
end)
```

title: System 18: Container/Inventory System
description:
Bags, chests, and containers with capacity and lock management (inspired by Evennia contribs).

## File Structure
```
lib/exmud/framework/inventory/
├── container.ex          # Container component and logic
└── container_locks.ex    # Lock/key mechanics
```

## Container Definition (YAML)
```yaml
# priv/world/items/leather_backpack.yml
key: leather_backpack
name: "Leather Backpack"
type: item
components:
  container:
    capacity: 20             # Max items (slots)
    weight_limit: 50         # Max total weight
    allowed_types: [item]    # What can go in (item, weapon, armor, all)
    locked: false
    key_item: null           # Item key needed to open
    open: true               # Currently open?
  physical:
    weight: 2
    size: medium
  equipable:
    slot: back               # Worn on back
description: "A sturdy leather backpack with many pockets."
```

## Lockable Container (YAML)
```yaml
# priv/world/items/treasure_chest.yml
key: treasure_chest
name: "Treasure Chest"
components:
  container:
    capacity: 30
    weight_limit: 100
    locked: true
    key_item: gold_key       # Requires this item to unlock
    lock_difficulty: 5       # For lockpicking skill
    open: false
  physical:
    weight: 20
    size: large
    movable: false           # Can't be picked up
```

## Container States
- **open**: Contents visible and accessible
- **closed**: Contents hidden, can be opened
- **locked**: Requires key or lockpicking to open
- **trapped**: (Optional) Triggers effect when opened

## Nested Containers
Containers can hold other containers (bags in bags):
```yaml
# Runtime example
leather_backpack:
  contents:
    - potion_pouch:        # Another container
        contents:
          - health_potion
          - mana_potion
    - sword
    - gold_coins
```

## Core Structs
```elixir
defmodule ExMUD.Framework.Inventory.Container do
  defstruct [
    :capacity,           # Max slots
    :weight_limit,       # Max weight
    :allowed_types,      # [item_type]
    :locked,             # Boolean
    :key_item,           # Item key for unlock
    :lock_difficulty,    # For lockpicking
    :open,               # Boolean
    :contents            # [entity_id]
  ]
end
```

## API Functions
- `Container.get_contents(container)` - List items inside
- `Container.can_add?(container, item)` - Check capacity/type/weight
- `Container.add(container, item)` - Put item in container
- `Container.remove(container, item)` - Take item from container
- `Container.get_weight(container)` - Total weight of contents
- `Container.get_free_slots(container)` - Available slots
- `Container.open(entity, container)` - Open container
- `Container.close(entity, container)` - Close container
- `Container.unlock(entity, container, key_item)` - Unlock with key
- `Container.lockpick(entity, container)` - Attempt lockpicking

## Integration Points
- Inventory system uses containers for player bags
- Room can have fixed containers (chests)
- Lock system integrates with skill checks
- Weight affects movement (if overloaded)
- Crafting can create containers

title: Implement EntityRegistry for On-Demand Process Management
description:
Create the EntityRegistry module that manages EntityServer processes on-demand.

## Context

The registry is the entry point for interacting with active entities. It:
- Looks up existing EntityServer processes
- Starts new processes on-demand when entity is accessed
- Tracks all active entity processes
- Provides broadcast to room occupants

## Files to Create

### `lib/exmud/engine/entity_registry.ex`

```elixir
defmodule Exmud.Engine.EntityRegistry do
  @moduledoc """
  Registry for active EntityServer processes.
  
  Provides on-demand process management - entities only become
  processes when they're accessed. Inactive processes stop themselves.
  
  ## Usage
  
      # Get or start an entity process
      {:ok, pid} = EntityRegistry.get_or_start(entity_id)
      
      # Check if entity is currently active
      case EntityRegistry.lookup(entity_id) do
        {:ok, pid} -> # Process exists
        :not_found -> # Entity is not active
      end
      
      # Broadcast event to all entities in a room
      EntityRegistry.broadcast_to_room(room_id, event)
  """

  use GenServer

  @registry_name Exmud.Engine.EntityRegistry.Registry
  @supervisor_name Exmud.Engine.EntitySupervisor

  # Client API
  def start_link(opts \\ [])
  def get_or_start(entity_id)
  def lookup(entity_id)
  def stop(entity_id)
  def list_active()
  def count_active()
  def broadcast_to_room(room_id, event)
  def broadcast_to_entity(entity_id, event)

  # GenServer for tracking room occupants
  def init(_opts)
  def handle_call({:register_in_room, entity_id, room_id}, _from, state)
  def handle_call({:unregister_from_room, entity_id, room_id}, _from, state)
  def handle_call({:get_room_occupants, room_id}, _from, state)
end
```

### `lib/exmud/engine/entity_supervisor.ex`

```elixir
defmodule Exmud.Engine.EntitySupervisor do
  @moduledoc """
  DynamicSupervisor for EntityServer processes.
  """

  use DynamicSupervisor

  def start_link(opts \\ [])
  def start_child(entity_id)
  def stop_child(entity_id)
end
```

## Key Functions

### `get_or_start/1`
```elixir
def get_or_start(entity_id) do
  case Registry.lookup(@registry_name, entity_id) do
    [{pid, _}] -> 
      {:ok, pid}
    [] -> 
      # Start new EntityServer
      case EntitySupervisor.start_child(entity_id) do
        {:ok, pid} -> {:ok, pid}
        {:error, {:already_started, pid}} -> {:ok, pid}
        error -> error
      end
  end
end
```

### `broadcast_to_room/2`
```elixir
def broadcast_to_room(room_id, event) do
  # Get room's contents from DB or cache
  contents = Entities.get_contents(room_id)
  
  # Send event to each active entity in room
  Enum.each(contents, fn entity ->
    case lookup(entity.id) do
      {:ok, pid} -> EntityServer.handle_event(pid, event)
      :not_found -> :ok  # Entity not active, skip
    end
  end)
end
```

## Supervision Tree Update

Add to `lib/exmud/application.ex`:

```elixir
children = [
  # ... existing children ...
  
  # Entity process management
  {Registry, keys: :unique, name: Exmud.Engine.EntityRegistry.Registry},
  {Exmud.Engine.EntitySupervisor, name: Exmud.Engine.EntitySupervisor},
  Exmud.Engine.EntityRegistry,
  
  # ... rest of children ...
]
```

## Room Occupancy Tracking

The registry also tracks which entities are in which rooms for efficient broadcast:

```elixir
# State: %{room_id => MapSet of entity_ids}
def init(_opts) do
  {:ok, %{rooms: %{}}}
end

def handle_call({:register_in_room, entity_id, room_id}, _from, state) do
  rooms = Map.update(state.rooms, room_id, MapSet.new([entity_id]), &MapSet.put(&1, entity_id))
  {:reply, :ok, %{state | rooms: rooms}}
end
```

## Tests

Create `test/exmud/engine/entity_registry_test.exs`:
- get_or_start creates new process
- get_or_start returns existing process
- lookup finds active process
- lookup returns :not_found for inactive
- stop terminates process
- list_active returns all active entity IDs
- broadcast_to_room sends to room occupants

title: System 21: Housing/Room Building System
description:
Players can create, customize, and own rooms with furniture and permissions.

## File Structure
```
lib/exmud/framework/housing/
├── player_room.ex        # Player-owned room logic
├── furniture.ex          # Furniture items and placement
├── housing_plot.ex       # Purchasable housing plots
└── permissions.ex        # Access control for rooms
```

## Housing Plot (in room prototype)
```yaml
# priv/world/rooms/housing_district.yml
key: housing_district
name: "Housing District"
components:
  housing_area:
    plots:
      - plot_id: plot_1
        price: 1000
        size: small          # small | medium | large
        owner: null          # Player ID when purchased
      - plot_id: plot_2
        price: 2500
        size: medium
        owner: null
```

## Player Room Definition
```yaml
# When player purchases plot, room created:
key: player_room_abc123
name: "Cozy Cottage"        # Player-customizable
prototype: base_player_room
owner_id: player_123
components:
  player_owned:
    owner_id: player_123
    plot_id: plot_1
    purchased_at: ~U[2024-01-15 12:00:00Z]
    upkeep_due: ~U[2024-02-15 12:00:00Z]
    upkeep_cost: 100         # Gold per month
  customizable:
    name: "Cozy Cottage"
    description: "Your personal retreat in the city."
    furniture: []            # Placed furniture
    decorations: []          # Decorative items
  permissions:
    can_enter: [owner, friends]
    can_use_storage: [owner]
    can_modify: [owner]
    friends_list: [player_456, player_789]
```

## Furniture Definition (YAML)
```yaml
# priv/world/furniture/storage_chest.yml
key: storage_chest
name: "Storage Chest"
type: furniture
placement_slot: floor        # floor | wall | ceiling | corner
provides:
  storage:
    slots: 20                # Extra inventory slots
  rest_bonus: 0              # Bonus to resting here
cost:
  gold: 100
  materials:
    - item: wood
      quantity: 5
purchase_message: "You purchase a sturdy storage chest."
placement_message: "You place the chest against the wall."
```

## Furniture Types & Bonuses
```yaml
furniture_bonuses:
  bed:
    rest_bonus: 20           # Faster HP regen when resting
    required_for: sleep      # Must have bed to sleep
  storage_chest:
    storage: 20              # Extra item slots
  workbench:
    crafting_station: workbench
  alchemy_table:
    crafting_station: alchemy
  bookshelf:
    skill_bonus: 5           # Bonus to study skills
  hearth:
    warmth: 10               # Protection from cold
    cooking_station: true
```

## Permission Types
- `can_enter` - Who can enter the room
- `can_use_storage` - Who can access storage furniture
- `can_modify` - Who can place/remove furniture
- `can_invite` - Who can add to friends list

## Permission Targets
- `owner` - Room owner only
- `friends` - Owner's friends list
- `guild` - Guild members (if applicable)
- `public` - Anyone

## Core Structs
```elixir
defmodule ExMUD.Framework.Housing.PlayerRoom do
  defstruct [
    :entity_id,
    :owner_id,
    :plot_id,
    :purchased_at,
    :upkeep_due,
    :upkeep_cost,
    :name,
    :description,
    :furniture,          # [{position, furniture_key, entity_id}]
    :permissions
  ]
end

defmodule ExMUD.Framework.Housing.Furniture do
  defstruct [
    :key,
    :name,
    :placement_slot,
    :provides,           # %{bonus_type => value}
    :cost
  ]
end
```

## API Functions
- `Housing.list_plots(room)` - Get available plots in area
- `Housing.purchase_plot(entity, plot_id)` - Buy a plot
- `Housing.get_player_room(entity)` - Get player's owned room
- `Housing.set_name(entity, room, name)` - Rename room
- `Housing.set_description(entity, room, desc)` - Change description
- `Furniture.place(entity, room, furniture, position)` - Place furniture
- `Furniture.remove(entity, room, position)` - Remove furniture
- `Furniture.get_bonuses(room)` - Calculate all bonuses
- `Permissions.can?(entity, room, action)` - Check permission
- `Permissions.set_friends(entity, room, friends)` - Update friends
- `Housing.pay_upkeep(entity, room)` - Pay monthly upkeep

## Integration Points
- Economy system for purchases
- Inventory for furniture items
- Storage extends inventory capacity
- Crafting stations in homes
- Rest system uses bed bonus
- Locks system for room access

title: Configure JWT token expiration
description:
No visible JWT expiration time configuration in Guardian.

File: lib/exmud/auth/guardian.ex

Impact: Tokens may have indefinite validity, which is a security risk.

Fix: Configure 'ttl' in Guardian config for token expiration:
```elixir
config :exmud, Exmud.Auth.Guardian,
  issuer: "exmud",
  ttl: {1, :day},  # or {4, :hours} for stricter security
  secret_key: ...
```

Also consider implementing refresh tokens for longer sessions.

title: Implement Entity Spawner from Prototypes
description:
Create the Spawner module that creates Entity records from Prototype templates.

## Context

The Spawner bridges prototypes (templates) and entities (database records). It:
- Creates new entities from prototype definitions
- Persists entities to the database
- Handles location placement
- Supports overrides for customization

## Current State

- `Exmud.Engine.Entities` handles entity CRUD
- `Exmud.Engine.Entity` is the in-memory struct
- Demo game has a Spawner but only for respawn timing

## Files to Create

### `lib/exmud/engine/spawner.ex`

```elixir
defmodule Exmud.Engine.Spawner do
  @moduledoc """
  Create entities from prototype templates.
  
  ## Usage
  
      # Spawn a goblin at a location
      {:ok, entity} = Spawner.spawn("goblin_warrior", location_id: room_id)
      
      # Spawn with overrides
      {:ok, entity} = Spawner.spawn("goblin_warrior", 
        location_id: room_id,
        name: "Goblin Champion",
        components: %{"combatant" => %{"level" => 5}}
      )
      
      # Spawn an entire room with its contents
      {:ok, room, spawned} = Spawner.spawn_room("forest_clearing")
  """

  alias Exmud.Engine.{Prototype, PrototypeLoader, Entities, Entity}

  def spawn(prototype_key, opts \\ [])
  def spawn_at(prototype_key, location_id, opts \\ [])
  def spawn_room(room_prototype_key, opts \\ [])
  def despawn(entity_id)  # Delete entity
end
```

## Key Functions

1. **`spawn/2`** - Create entity from prototype with options
   - Options: `:location_id`, `:name`, `:description`, `:components`, `:attributes`
   - Returns `{:ok, entity}` or `{:error, reason}`

2. **`spawn_at/3`** - Convenience for spawn with location

3. **`spawn_room/2`** - Spawn room and all entities defined in its `:spawns`
   - Creates room entity
   - Creates exit entities for each direction
   - Creates NPC/item entities from spawns list
   - Returns `{:ok, room, spawned_entities}`

4. **`despawn/1`** - Delete an entity (for cleanup)

## Entity Creation Flow

```
Prototype -> merge overrides -> Entity struct -> Entities.create_entity -> DB record
```

## Integration Points

- Call `PrototypeLoader.get/1` to fetch prototype
- Call `Prototype.to_entity/2` to convert with overrides
- Call `Entities.save_entity/1` to persist
- Optionally start EntityServer process (if implemented)

## Tests to Write

Create `test/exmud/engine/spawner_test.exs`:
- Spawn entity from valid prototype
- Spawn with overrides applied correctly
- Spawn at location sets location_id
- Spawn room creates room + exits + contents
- Spawn fails gracefully for unknown prototype

title: Update Application Supervision Tree for Engine Core
description:
Update the application.ex supervision tree to include all new engine core components.

## Context

After implementing the new engine modules, they need to be added to the supervision tree in the correct order.

## Current State

`lib/exmud/application.ex` currently has:
```elixir
children = [
  ExmudWeb.Telemetry,
  Exmud.Repo,
  {Ecto.Migrator, ...},
  {DNSCluster, ...},
  {Phoenix.PubSub, name: Exmud.PubSub},
  Exmud.DemoGame.Systems.Spawner,  # OLD - to be replaced
  ExmudWeb.Endpoint
]
```

## Required Changes

Update to:
```elixir
children = [
  ExmudWeb.Telemetry,
  Exmud.Repo,
  {Ecto.Migrator, repos: Application.fetch_env!(:exmud, :ecto_repos), skip: skip_migrations?()},
  {DNSCluster, query: Application.get_env(:exmud, :dns_cluster_query) || :ignore},
  {Phoenix.PubSub, name: Exmud.PubSub},
  
  # Engine Core - New Components
  Exmud.Engine.Hooks,                    # Lifecycle hooks registry
  Exmud.Engine.PrototypeLoader,          # Load YAML prototypes into ETS
  {Registry, keys: :unique, name: Exmud.Engine.EntityRegistry.Registry},
  {Exmud.Engine.EntitySupervisor, name: Exmud.Engine.EntitySupervisor},
  Exmud.Engine.EntityRegistry,           # Entity process management
  
  # Web endpoint - must be last
  ExmudWeb.Endpoint
]
```

## Post-Startup Hook

Add world loading after supervision tree starts:

```elixir
def start(_type, _args) do
  children = [...]
  opts = [strategy: :one_for_one, name: Exmud.Supervisor]
  
  case Supervisor.start_link(children, opts) do
    {:ok, pid} ->
      # Load world on startup if empty
      load_world_if_empty()
      {:ok, pid}
    error ->
      error
  end
end

defp load_world_if_empty do
  if Exmud.Engine.Entities.count_all() == 0 do
    Logger.info("Empty database, loading world from prototypes...")
    Exmud.Engine.WorldLoader.spawn_world()
  end
end
```

## Order Matters

1. **Hooks** - Must start first, other modules may register hooks
2. **PrototypeLoader** - Must start before WorldLoader can spawn
3. **Registry** - Must exist before EntitySupervisor
4. **EntitySupervisor** - Must exist before EntityRegistry
5. **EntityRegistry** - Depends on Registry and Supervisor
6. **Endpoint** - Always last

## Files to Modify

- `lib/exmud/application.ex`

## Testing

- Application starts without errors
- All new processes are running
- `Process.whereis(Exmud.Engine.Hooks)` returns pid
- `Process.whereis(Exmud.Engine.PrototypeLoader)` returns pid
- `Process.whereis(Exmud.Engine.EntityRegistry)` returns pid

Create modules to load the world from YAML prototypes and export world state back to YAML.

### `lib/exmud/engine/world_loader.ex`

```elixir
defmodule Exmud.Engine.WorldLoader do
  @moduledoc """
  Load and initialize game world from YAML prototypes.

end
```

### `lib/exmud/engine/world_exporter.ex`

```elixir
defmodule Exmud.Engine.WorldExporter do
  @moduledoc """
  Export world state to YAML files.
  
  ## Usage
  
      # Export all entities to YAML
      {:ok, path} = WorldExporter.export_all("priv/exports/backup_2024")
      
      # Export specific types
      {:ok, path} = WorldExporter.export_rooms("priv/exports/rooms")
      
      # Export single entity

  """

  def export_npcs(output_dir)
  def export_items(output_dir)
  def entity_to_yaml(entity)
  def entity_to_prototype(entity)

```

## World Loading Process

```elixir
def spawn_world(opts \\ []) do
  starting_room = Keyword.get(opts, :starting_room, @starting_room)
  
  # 1. Ensure prototypes are loaded
  PrototypeLoader.load_all()
  
  # 2. Spawn rooms in connected order (BFS from starting room)
  {:ok, rooms} = spawn_room_chain(starting_room)
  
  # 3. Spawn NPCs and items in each room
  spawned = Enum.flat_map(rooms, fn room ->
    spawn_room_contents(room)
  end)
  
  {:ok, %{rooms: length(rooms), entities: length(spawned)}}
end

def spawn_room_chain(starting_key, opts \\ []) do
  visited = MapSet.new()
  queue = :queue.from_list([starting_key])
  rooms = []
  
  # BFS through room exits
  spawn_rooms_bfs(queue, visited, rooms)
end
```

title: Integrate GameLive with New Engine Core
description:
Update the GameLive module to use the new engine core components (EntityRegistry, Hooks, etc.).

## Context

The game client (GameLive) needs to be updated to work with the new engine architecture:
- Use EntityRegistry to get/start room processes
- Interact with EntityServers instead of direct DB access
- Trigger hooks at appropriate points

## Current State

`lib/exmud_web/live/game_live.ex` currently:
- Loads rooms directly from database
- Uses RoomLoader for formatting
- Has PlayerGameState for player data
- Subscribes to PubSub topics manually

## Required Changes

### Room Loading

```elixir
# Before
defp load_room(room_id) do
  RoomLoader.load_room_for_display(room_id)
end

# After
defp load_room(room_id) do
  case EntityRegistry.get_or_start(room_id) do
    {:ok, pid} ->
      entity = EntityServer.get_entity(pid)
      format_room_for_display(entity)
    {:error, _} ->
      empty_room()
  end
end
```

### Player Movement

```elixir
def handle_event("move", %{"direction" => direction}, socket) do
  player = socket.assigns.current_player
  current_room = socket.assigns.room
  
  case get_exit(current_room, direction) do
    nil -> 
      {:noreply, put_flash(socket, :error, "You can't go that way.")}
    destination_id ->
      # Run before_move hook (can halt)
      case Hooks.run_until_halt(:at_before_move, [player, destination_id]) do
        :ok ->
          # Leave current room
          Hooks.run(:at_leave_room, [player, current_room.id])
          
          # Enter new room
          {:ok, new_room} = load_room(destination_id)
          Hooks.run(:at_enter_room, [player, destination_id])
          
          # Update socket
          {:noreply, assign(socket, room: new_room)}
        {:halt, reason} ->
          {:noreply, put_flash(socket, :error, reason)}
      end
  end
end
```

### Entity Interactions

```elixir
def handle_event("interact", %{"entity_id" => entity_id}, socket) do
  case EntityRegistry.get_or_start(entity_id) do
    {:ok, pid} ->
      EntityServer.touch(pid)  # Reset idle timer
      entity = EntityServer.get_entity(pid)
      handle_entity_interaction(socket, entity)
    {:error, reason} ->
      {:noreply, put_flash(socket, :error, "Cannot interact: #{reason}")}
  end
end
```

## Files to Modify

- `lib/exmud_web/live/game_live.ex`

title: Implement String-Based Locks System
description:
Create a Locks module that provides Evennia-style string-based access control.

## Context

Evennia uses lock strings like `"get:perm(builder) OR attr(strength, 50)"` for flexible access control. We need a similar system that:
- Parses lock definition strings
- Evaluates lock functions against accessor
- Supports AND/OR/NOT logic
- Is extensible with custom lock functions

## Current State

- Entity has a `locks` field (currently unused or basic)
- No lock parsing or evaluation exists
- Access control is ad-hoc in code

## Files to Create

### `lib/exmud/engine/locks.ex`

```elixir
defmodule Exmud.Engine.Locks do
  @moduledoc """
  String-based access control system.
  
  ## Lock String Format
  
      access_type:lockfunc(args) [AND|OR] lockfunc2(args)
  
  ## Examples
  
      "get:all()"                           # Anyone can get
      "get:none()"                          # No one can get
      "edit:perm(admin)"                    # Only admins can edit
      "traverse:has_key(gold_key)"          # Need gold_key item
      "get:attr_gt(strength, 50)"           # Strength > 50 to get
      "delete:id(123) OR perm(admin)"       # Owner or admin
      "use:perm(builder) AND NOT tag(broken)" # Builder, not broken
  
  ## Usage
  
      # Check access
      case Locks.check(chest, player, "get") do
        :ok -> allow_get()
        {:denied, reason} -> deny_with_message(reason)
      end
      
      # Set locks on entity
      entity = Entity.set_attribute(entity, "locks", %{
        "get" => "perm(builder) OR attr(strength, 50)",
        "edit" => "perm(admin)",
        "delete" => "id(#{owner_id})"
      })
  """

  # Built-in lock functions
  @lock_functions %{
    "all" => &__MODULE__.check_all/3,
    "none" => &__MODULE__.check_none/3,
    "perm" => &__MODULE__.check_permission/3,
    "attr" => &__MODULE__.check_attribute/3,
    "attr_gt" => &__MODULE__.check_attribute_gt/3,
    "attr_lt" => &__MODULE__.check_attribute_lt/3,
    "id" => &__MODULE__.check_id/3,
    "tag" => &__MODULE__.check_tag/3,
    "has_item" => &__MODULE__.check_has_item/3,
    "has_key" => &__MODULE__.check_has_key/3,
    "in_room" => &__MODULE__.check_in_room/3,
    "is_type" => &__MODULE__.check_is_type/3
  }

  # Public API
  def check(entity, accessor, access_type)
  def parse(lock_string)
  def evaluate(parsed_lock, entity, accessor)
  def register_function(name, fun)
  def get_lock(entity, access_type)
  def set_lock(entity, access_type, lock_string)

  # Lock Functions (entity, accessor, args)
  def check_all(_entity, _accessor, _args), do: true
  def check_none(_entity, _accessor, _args), do: false
  def check_permission(_entity, accessor, [perm_name])
  def check_attribute(entity, _accessor, [attr_name, expected_value])
  def check_attribute_gt(entity, _accessor, [attr_name, threshold])
  def check_id(_entity, accessor, [id])
  def check_tag(entity, _accessor, [tag_name])
  def check_has_item(_entity, accessor, [item_key])
end
```

## Lock Parsing

```elixir
# Parse "perm(admin) OR attr(strength, 50)" into AST
def parse(lock_string) do
  lock_string
  |> tokenize()
  |> parse_expression()
end

# Tokenize into: [{:func, "perm", ["admin"]}, :or, {:func, "attr", ["strength", "50"]}]
defp tokenize(string)

# Parse into: {:or, {:func, "perm", ["admin"]}, {:func, "attr", ["strength", "50"]}}
defp parse_expression(tokens)
```

## Lock Evaluation

```elixir
def evaluate({:and, left, right}, entity, accessor) do
  evaluate(left, entity, accessor) and evaluate(right, entity, accessor)
end

def evaluate({:or, left, right}, entity, accessor) do
  evaluate(left, entity, accessor) or evaluate(right, entity, accessor)
end

def evaluate({:not, expr}, entity, accessor) do
  not evaluate(expr, entity, accessor)
end

def evaluate({:func, name, args}, entity, accessor) do
  case Map.get(@lock_functions, name) do
    nil -> false  # Unknown function = deny
    fun -> fun.(entity, accessor, args)
  end
end
```

## Integration with Entity

```elixir
# In Entity module, add convenience functions
def can_access?(entity, accessor, access_type) do
  Locks.check(entity, accessor, access_type) == :ok
end
```

## Tests

Create `test/exmud/engine/locks_test.exs`:
- Parse simple lock strings
- Parse AND/OR/NOT combinations
- check_permission works with player perms
- check_attribute compares values
- check_attribute_gt/lt for numeric comparison
- check_id matches accessor ID
- check_tag finds entity tags
- check_has_item looks in inventory
- Complex expressions evaluate correctly
- Unknown functions deny access
design: Parse lock strings into AST for efficient repeated evaluation. Lock functions receive (entity, accessor, args). Results are cached per request if needed. Custom functions can be registered at runtime.

- [ ] check/3 returns :ok or {:denied, reason}
- [ ] register_function/2 adds custom functions
- [ ] Entity integration helpers added
- [ ] Tests pass

title: System 9: Barter/Trading System
description:
Safe player-to-player item and gold exchange.

## File Structure
```
lib/exmud/framework/trading/
├── trade.ex              # Trade session management
└── trade_window.ex       # Trade state and UI data
```

## Trade Configuration (YAML)
```yaml
# config/trading.yml
trading:
  max_items_per_trade: 10
  timeout_seconds: 300       # Auto-cancel after 5 min
  require_both_confirm: true
  trade_log: true            # Log all trades
  allow_gold: true
  allow_bound_items: false   # Soulbound items can't be traded
```

## Core Structs
```elixir
defmodule ExMUD.Framework.Trading.TradeSession do
  defstruct [
    :id,
    :initiator_id,
    :target_id,
    :initiator_offer,    # %TradeOffer{}
    :target_offer,       # %TradeOffer{}
    :initiator_confirmed,
    :target_confirmed,
    :status,             # :pending | :confirmed | :completed | :cancelled
    :started_at,
    :timeout_at
  ]
end

defmodule ExMUD.Framework.Trading.TradeOffer do
  defstruct [
    :items,              # [{item_id, quantity}]
    :gold,               # Amount of gold
    :confirmed           # Boolean
  ]
end
```

## Trade Flow
1. Player A initiates: `TRADE offer <player B>`
2. Player B accepts: `TRADE accept`
3. Both add items: `TRADE add <item>` or `TRADE add gold 100`
4. Both can remove: `TRADE remove <item>`
5. Both confirm: `TRADE confirm`
6. Exchange happens atomically
7. Either can cancel anytime: `TRADE cancel`

## API Functions
- `Trade.initiate(initiator, target)` - Start trade session
- `Trade.accept(target)` - Accept trade invitation
- `Trade.add_item(entity, item_id, quantity)` - Add to offer
- `Trade.add_gold(entity, amount)` - Add gold to offer
- `Trade.remove_item(entity, item_id)` - Remove from offer
- `Trade.confirm(entity)` - Lock in offer
- `Trade.execute(session)` - Perform exchange (internal)
- `Trade.cancel(entity)` - Abort trade
- `TradeWindow.get_state(session, for_entity)` - UI data

## Trade Display Format
```
=== Trade with Pema ===
You offer:           | Pema offers:
  Iron Sword         |   Health Potion x3
  50 gold            |   Leather Gloves
                     |
[Your offer: CONFIRMED] [Pema's offer: PENDING]
```

## Integration Points
- Inventory system for item transfer
- Events for trade notifications
- Logging for audit trail

Rooms have elements (water, fire, stone) that interact with abilities and weather.

name: "Waterfall Cave"
description: "Water cascades down the rock face..."

  room_elements:

      intensity: high        # none | low | medium | high

    vegetation:
      intensity: low

    # How abilities interact with this room

    lightning:
      effectiveness: +25     # Lightning stronger (water conducts)

    ice:
      special: freeze_water  # Special effect - freeze the waterfall

```

elements:

weather_element_effects:

title: System 3: Status Effects System
description:
Build a comprehensive buff/debuff/condition system with triggers, durations, and cures.

**Reference:** Plan file Section "System 7: Status Effects System"

## Files to Create

```
lib/exmud/framework/status/
├── status_effect.ex     # Status effect definition struct
└── status_manager.ex    # Apply/remove/tick status effects on entities
```

## Status Effect Struct

```elixir
%StatusEffect{
  key: "poisoned",
  name: "Poisoned",
  type: :debuff,  # :buff | :debuff | :neutral
  duration: 5,     # turns, or nil for permanent until cured
  stackable: false,
  max_stacks: 1,
  effects: [
    %{trigger: :on_turn_start, effect: :damage, amount: 5, damage_type: :poison},
    %{trigger: :passive, effect: :stat_modify, stat: :str, modifier: -2}
  ],
  cure_items: ["antidote"],
  cure_abilities: ["cure_poison", "greater_heal"],
  display_icon: "poison",
  display_color: "green",
  description: "Poison courses through your veins."
}
```

## Effect Triggers

1. `:on_apply` - When first applied
2. `:on_remove` - When removed/expires
3. `:on_turn_start` - Each turn start
4. `:on_turn_end` - Each turn end
5. `:on_damage_taken` - When receiving damage
6. `:on_damage_dealt` - When dealing damage
7. `:on_ability_use` - When using any ability
8. `:passive` - Constant effect (stat modifiers)

## Effect Actions

- `:damage` - Deal damage {amount, damage_type}
- `:heal` - Restore HP {amount}
- `:stat_modify` - Modify stat {stat, modifier}
- `:resource_drain` - Drain resource {resource, amount}
- `:prevent_action` - Prevent action type {action_type} (stun, silence)
- `:reflect_damage` - Reflect % of damage taken {percentage}
- `:immunity` - Immune to damage type or status

## YAML Format

```yaml
# priv/world/statuses/poisoned.yml
key: poisoned
name: "Poisoned"
type: debuff
duration: 5
stackable: false
effects:
  - trigger: on_turn_start
    effect: damage
    amount: 5
    damage_type: poison
  - trigger: passive
    effect: stat_modify
    stat: str
    modifier: -2
cure_items: [antidote]
cure_abilities: [cure_poison, greater_heal]
display_icon: poison
display_color: green
description: "Poison courses through your veins."
```

## Item Status Triggers

Items can apply status effects:

```yaml
# In item definition
components:
  equipable:
    slot: weapon
    on_equip:
      - apply_status: poison_immunity
    on_hit:
      - apply_status: poisoned
        chance: 0.3
```

## API Functions

```elixir
StatusEffect.Registry.get(status_key)

StatusManager.apply(entity_id, status_key, source_id, opts \\ [])
StatusManager.remove(entity_id, status_key)
StatusManager.has?(entity_id, status_key)
StatusManager.get_active(entity_id)
StatusManager.get_stacks(entity_id, status_key)
StatusManager.tick(entity_id)  # Process turn-based effects
StatusManager.try_cure(entity_id, status_key, cure_source)
StatusManager.get_stat_modifiers(entity_id, stat)  # Sum all passive mods
```

## Integration Points

- Extend PrototypeLoader to load `priv/world/statuses/*.yml`
- Add `active_statuses` to player GameState
- Called by Ability System to apply status effects
- Called by Combat System on damage events
- Called by Item System on equip/hit events
- Stat calculations must query passive modifiers
close_reason: Implemented status effects system with 3 core modules: StatusEffect (definition struct), StatusRegistry (YAML loading), StatusManager (apply/remove/tick/cure). Added 6 sample statuses (poisoned, burning, blessed, stunned, regenerating, shielded). All 476 tests pass.

title: Engine Core Hardening - Evennia-Inspired Architecture
description:
Harden ExMUD's engine core to support a three-layer architecture inspired by Evennia (Python MUD framework). This creates a solid foundation that is LLM-friendly and enables seamless evolution of a living game world.

## Architecture Goal

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ LAYER 3: WORLD DATA (priv/world/)                               │
│   YAML prototypes for rooms, NPCs, items, quests                │
│   Data-driven content creation (LLM-friendly)                   │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ LAYER 2: GAME FRAMEWORK (lib/exmud/framework/)                  │
│   Combat, quests, dialogue, inventory, skills                   │
│   Reusable game mechanics with configuration                    │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ LAYER 1: ENGINE CORE (lib/exmud/engine/)                        │
│   Entity, Event, Behavior, Command, Prototype, Hooks, Locks     │
│   Stable foundation that rarely changes                         │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

## Key Decisions Made

- **Prototype Storage**: YAML files only (version controlled, LLM-friendly)
- **Entity Processes**: Hybrid on-demand GenServers for rooms/NPCs only
- **Demo Content**: Start fresh (expendable during refactor)

## Reference Documentation

- Plan file: ~/.claude/plans/parallel-wobbling-stroustrup.md
- Evennia docs: https://www.evennia.com/docs/latest/
- Current engine: server/lib/exmud/engine/

## Success Criteria

1. Entities can be created from YAML prototypes without code
2. Active rooms/NPCs run as supervised GenServer processes
3. Framework layer can hook into engine lifecycle events
4. String-based locks system for access control
5. World can be loaded from and exported to YAML files

title: System 23: Spell Words System (LegendMUD-Style)
description:
LegendMUD-inspired syllable-based magic system where players combine words to create spells.

## Overview
Instead of learning discrete spells, players learn magical syllables (words) and combine them to create effects. This is an OPTIONAL advanced system that can be used alongside or instead of the standard Ability System.

## File Structure
```
lib/exmud/framework/spellwords/
├── spell_word.ex         # Word definitions
├── spell_combination.ex  # Valid combinations
└── spell_casting.ex      # Casting logic
```

## Spell Word Types
```yaml
# priv/world/spellwords/words.yml
words:
  # Verbs (required, always first position)
  kre:
    type: verb
    meaning: create
    mana_cost: 5
    learn_from: [archmage, ancient_tome]
  des:
    type: verb
    meaning: destroy
    mana_cost: 8
  mut:
    type: verb
    meaning: change/transform
    mana_cost: 6
  mov:
    type: verb
    meaning: move/teleport
    mana_cost: 10
  sen:
    type: verb
    meaning: sense/detect
    mana_cost: 3

  # Elements (modifiers, second position)
  fir:
    type: element
    meaning: fire
    mana_cost: 5
    damage_type: fire
  aqu:
    type: element
    meaning: water
    mana_cost: 4
  ter:
    type: element
    meaning: earth
    mana_cost: 4
  aer:
    type: element
    meaning: air
    mana_cost: 3
  lux:
    type: element
    meaning: light
    mana_cost: 4
  nox:
    type: element
    meaning: darkness
    mana_cost: 5
  vit:
    type: element
    meaning: life
    mana_cost: 6

  # Targets (third position)
  sel:
    type: target
    meaning: self
    mana_cost: 0
  hos:
    type: target
    meaning: enemy/hostile
    mana_cost: 2
  ami:
    type: target
    meaning: ally/friend
    mana_cost: 1
  loc:
    type: target
    meaning: location/area
    mana_cost: 3
  obj:
    type: target
    meaning: object
    mana_cost: 1
```

## Spell Combinations
```yaml
# priv/world/spellwords/combinations.yml
combinations:
  - words: [kre, fir, hos]     # create + fire + enemy
    result: fireball
    effect:
      type: damage
      amount: 25
      damage_type: fire
    description: "Conjures flames and hurls them at the target."
    cast_message: "You speak the words of power: KRE FIR HOS!"

  - words: [mut, aqu, sel]     # change + water + self
    result: water_breathing
    effect:
      type: buff
      status: water_breathing
      duration: 300
    description: "Allows breathing underwater."

  - words: [des, ter, loc]     # destroy + earth + location
    result: earthquake
    effect:
      type: area_damage
      amount: 15
      targets: all_in_room
    description: "Shakes the ground violently."

  - words: [kre, vit, ami]     # create + life + ally
    result: heal
    effect:
      type: heal
      amount: 30
    description: "Restores life force to an ally."

  - words: [sen, nox, loc]     # sense + darkness + location
    result: detect_hidden
    effect:
      type: reveal
      reveals: [hidden_entities, secret_exits]
    description: "Reveals hidden things in the shadows."
```

## Learning Words
Words are learned from:
- NPC teachers (mages, sages)
- Ancient texts (quest items)
- Magical discoveries
- Meditation at power sites

## Player Known Words
```yaml
# In player entity components
components:
  spellwords:
    known_words: [kre, fir, aqu, sel, hos]
    word_mastery:
      kre: 80                # Mastery affects power
      fir: 65
```

## Core Structs
```elixir
defmodule ExMUD.Framework.Spellwords.Word do
  defstruct [
    :key,
    :type,               # :verb | :element | :target
    :meaning,
    :mana_cost,
    :learn_from
  ]
end

defmodule ExMUD.Framework.Spellwords.Combination do
  defstruct [
    :words,              # [word_key]
    :result,             # Spell name
    :effect,
    :description,
    :cast_message
  ]
end
```

## Casting
```
CHANT kre fir hos        # Cast fireball at enemy
CHANT mut aqu sel        # Cast water breathing on self
CHANT kre vit ami        # Heal an ally
```

## Invalid Combinations
When words don't form a valid combination:
```
> CHANT kre kre fir
The words clash discordantly. Nothing happens.
(You lose half the mana cost)
```

## API Functions
- `Spellwords.get_known_words(entity)` - Player's known words
- `Spellwords.learn_word(entity, word_key, source)` - Learn new word
- `Spellwords.can_cast?(entity, words)` - Check if valid + mana
- `Spellwords.cast(entity, words, target)` - Execute spell
- `Spellwords.get_combination(words)` - Get spell for word combo
- `Spellwords.list_known_combinations(entity)` - All castable spells

## Integration Points
- Resource system for mana consumption
- Status effects for buff spells
- Combat for damage spells
- Skill system for word mastery
- Teachers for learning words
- Quest items for rare words

description:
Refactor the monolithic GameLive.ex (1,566 lines) into focused modules.

## Current state
- `lib/exmud_web/live/game_live.ex` - 1,566 lines
- Contains: mount, room loading, combat, inventory, dialogue, movement handlers
- All event handlers in one file

## Target structure
```
lib/exmud_web/live/game_live/
├── game_live.ex          # Main module: mount, socket setup, routing (~300 lines)
├── room_manager.ex       # Room loading, player movement, entity display
├── combat_manager.ex     # Combat event handlers, action processing
├── inventory_manager.ex  # Inventory/equipment event handlers
├── dialogue_manager.ex   # NPC dialogue event handlers
└── components.ex         # Keep as-is (UI components, already extracted)
```

## Approach
1. Create new modules as Phoenix.LiveView helpers (not full LiveViews)
2. Move related event handlers to appropriate modules
3. Keep main game_live.ex as the coordinator
4. Use `defdelegate` or direct function calls

## Example pattern
```elixir
# In game_live.ex
def handle_event("attack", params, socket) do
  CombatManager.handle_attack(params, socket)
end

# Or use Phoenix.LiveView helpers
use GameLive.CombatManager
```

## Files
- `lib/exmud_web/live/game_live.ex` (refactor, reduce to ~300 lines)
- `lib/exmud_web/live/game_live/room_manager.ex` (new)

title: System 22: Mail/Messaging System
description:
Inter-player and system messaging with attachments (inspired by Evennia contribs).

## File Structure
```
lib/exmud/framework/mail/
├── mail.ex               # Mail message handling
├── mailbox.ex            # Player mailbox management
└── mail_attachments.ex   # Item attachment logic
```

## Mail Configuration (YAML)
```yaml
# config/mail.yml
mail:
  max_inbox: 50              # Max messages per player
  retention_days: 30         # Auto-delete after
  attachments: true          # Allow item attachments
  cost_per_mail: 5           # Gold cost to send
  cod_enabled: true          # Cash-on-delivery
  max_attachments: 5         # Items per message
  system_sender: "System"    # Name for system messages
```

## Mail Message Schema
```yaml
# Example mail message
id: mail_abc123
from_id: player_456
from_name: "Tenzin"
to_id: player_123
subject: "A gift for you"
body: |
  I found this rare item and thought of you.
  May it aid your journey.
  
  - Tenzin
attachments:
  - item_id: rare_sword_instance
    cod_price: null          # Not COD, free gift
read: false
sent_at: ~U[2024-01-20 14:30:00Z]
expires_at: ~U[2024-02-19 14:30:00Z]
```

## COD (Cash on Delivery)
```yaml
# COD message example
attachments:
  - item_id: magic_ring_instance
    cod_price: 500           # Must pay 500 gold to receive
```

## System Messages
```yaml
# Automated system messages
from_id: null                # null = system message
from_name: "System"
subject: "Quest Reward"
body: "Congratulations on completing 'The Three Trials'!"
attachments:
  - item_id: quest_reward_item
```

## Core Structs
```elixir
defmodule ExMUD.Framework.Mail.Message do
  defstruct [
    :id,
    :from_id,
    :from_name,
    :to_id,
    :subject,
    :body,
    :attachments,        # [{item_id, cod_price}]
    :read,
    :sent_at,
    :expires_at
  ]
end

defmodule ExMUD.Framework.Mail.Mailbox do
  defstruct [
    :owner_id,
    :messages,           # [Message.t()]
    :unread_count
  ]
end
```

## Commands
```
MAIL                     # View inbox
MAIL read                # Read oldest unread
MAIL read 3              # Read message #3
MAIL send <player>       # Start composing
MAIL subject <text>      # Set subject
MAIL body <text>         # Set body
MAIL attach <item>       # Attach item
MAIL cod <amount>        # Set COD price for last attachment
MAIL send                # Send the message
MAIL reply <id>          # Reply to message
MAIL delete <id>         # Delete message
MAIL claim <id>          # Claim attachments (pay COD if needed)
```

## API Functions
- `Mail.send(from, to, subject, body, attachments)` - Send message
- `Mail.send_system(to, subject, body, attachments)` - System message
- `Mail.get_inbox(entity)` - Get all messages
- `Mail.get_unread(entity)` - Get unread messages
- `Mail.read(entity, message_id)` - Mark as read
- `Mail.claim_attachments(entity, message_id)` - Take items
- `Mail.delete(entity, message_id)` - Delete message
- `Mail.reply(entity, message_id, body)` - Reply to message
- `Mailbox.cleanup_expired(entity)` - Remove old messages

## Integration Points
- Inventory for attachments
- Economy for mail cost and COD
- Quest system sends reward mail
- Events trigger system notifications
- Offline players receive mail when they log in

title: Implement YAML Prototype Loader
description:
Create the PrototypeLoader module that reads YAML files from disk and builds an in-memory registry of prototypes.

## Context

Prototypes are stored as YAML files in `priv/world/prototypes/`. This loader:
- Reads all YAML files from the prototype directories
- Parses and validates each prototype
- Resolves parent inheritance chains
- Stores prototypes in ETS for fast lookup

## Directory Structure

```
priv/world/prototypes/
├── rooms/
│   ├── town_square.yml
│   └── dark_forest.yml
├── npcs/
│   ├── base_npc.yml      # Parent prototype
│   ├── goblin.yml
│   └── merchant.yml
├── items/
│   ├── base_weapon.yml
│   └── rusty_sword.yml
└── exits/
    └── standard_exit.yml
```

## YAML Format Example

```yaml
# priv/world/prototypes/npcs/goblin.yml
key: goblin_warrior
parent: base_npc
type: npc
name: "Goblin Warrior"
description: |
  A fierce goblin wielding a rusty sword.
  Its beady eyes watch you with hostility.
components:
  combatant:
    health:
      current: 30
      max: 30
    stats:
      str: 8
      dex: 12
      sta: 6
    level: 2
behaviors:
  - Exmud.Framework.Combat.AggressiveBehavior
attributes:
  respawn_time: 300
  loot_table: goblin_loot
tags:
  - hostile
  - goblinoid
```

## Files to Create

### `lib/exmud/engine/prototype_loader.ex`

```elixir
defmodule Exmud.Engine.PrototypeLoader do
  @moduledoc """
  Loads prototypes from YAML files into ETS registry.
  """

  @prototype_table :exmud_prototypes
  @default_path "priv/world/prototypes"

  def start_link(opts \\ [])
  def load_all(path \\ @default_path)
  def reload()
  def get(key)
  def list_by_type(type)
  def all()
  def validate_all()  # Check for broken references
end
```

## Key Functions

1. **`start_link/1`** - Start GenServer that owns ETS table
2. **`load_all/1`** - Recursively load all YAML files from directory
3. **`reload/0`** - Clear and reload all prototypes (hot-reload)
4. **`get/1`** - Fetch prototype by key (with parent resolution)
5. **`list_by_type/1`** - Get all prototypes of a type
6. **`validate_all/0`** - Check for broken parent references, cycles

## Dependencies

Add to `mix.exs`:
```elixir
{:yaml_elixir, "~> 2.9"}
```

## Implementation Notes

- Use ETS for fast concurrent reads
- GenServer holds ETS table ownership
- Parent resolution is done at load time, not lookup time
- Behavior module atoms must be validated (module exists)
- File watching for dev-time hot-reload (optional)
design: GenServer owns ETS table for prototype storage. Load order: base prototypes first (no parent), then children. Use topological sort if needed for complex inheritance. Cache resolved prototypes (with parents merged) for fast lookup.

title: Implement Prototype Struct and Validation
description:
Create the Prototype module that defines templates for spawning entities. This is the foundation of the data-driven content system.

## Context

Evennia uses "prototypes" - dictionary templates that define object properties. We're implementing an Elixir equivalent using structs and YAML files. This enables:
- Non-coders to create game content
- LLMs to generate world data
- Version-controlled content definitions

## Current State

- Entity struct exists at `lib/exmud/engine/entity.ex`
- No prototype/template system exists
- Entities are created programmatically or via admin UI

## Files to Create

### `lib/exmud/engine/prototype.ex`

```elixir
defmodule Exmud.Engine.Prototype do
  @moduledoc """
  Template for spawning entities without code.
  
  Prototypes define the default properties for an entity type.
  They support inheritance via the :parent field.
  
  ## Example
  
      %Prototype{
        key: "goblin_warrior",
        parent: "base_npc",
        type: :npc,
        name: "Goblin Warrior",
        description: "A fierce goblin wielding a rusty sword.",
        components: %{
          "combatant" => %{"health" => %{"current" => 30, "max" => 30}}
        },
        tags: ["hostile", "goblinoid"]
      }
  """

  @enforce_keys [:key, :type]
  defstruct [
    :key,              # Unique identifier (e.g., "goblin_warrior")
    :parent,           # Inherits from another prototype key
    :type,             # :room | :npc | :item | :exit | :character
    :name,
    :description,
    :components,       # Map of component_name => component_data
    :behaviors,        # List of behavior module atoms
    :attributes,       # Map of key => value
    :tags,             # List of string tags
    :scripts,          # Map of hook => script_source
    :locks,            # Map of access_type => lock_string
    :exits,            # For rooms: %{"north" => "room_key", ...}
    :spawns            # For rooms: list of entity prototypes to spawn here
  ]

  @valid_types [:room, :npc, :item, :exit, :character]

  def new(attrs)
  def validate(prototype)
  def merge_parent(child, parent_prototype)
  def to_entity(prototype, overrides \\ %{})
  def from_map(map)  # Convert from YAML-parsed map
end
```

1. **`new/1`** - Create prototype from keyword list
2. **`validate/1`** - Check required fields, valid types, reference integrity

4. **`to_entity/2`** - Convert prototype to Entity struct with optional overrides
5. **`from_map/1`** - Convert YAML-parsed map (string keys) to Prototype struct

- `:key` must be non-empty string, valid identifier
- `:type` must be one of @valid_types
- If `:parent` is set, it must reference an existing prototype
- `:components` must be a map with string keys
- `:behaviors` must be list of valid module atoms

title: Implement EntityServer GenServer for Active Entities
description:
Create the EntityServer GenServer that manages state for active room and NPC entities.

## Context

Currently ExMUD has NO GenServers for entities - all state is in the database. This task implements the hybrid on-demand approach:
- Entities start as DB records
- When accessed, a GenServer process is started
- Process holds live state, auto-saves periodically
- After inactivity, process hibernates or stops

## Benefits

- **Real-time NPC AI**: Mobs can think/act on tick intervals
- **Fast state access**: No DB query for hot data
- **Event handling**: Process receives and handles events
- **Memory efficient**: Only active areas have processes

## Files to Create

### `lib/exmud/engine/entity_server.ex`

```elixir
defmodule Exmud.Engine.EntityServer do
  @moduledoc """
  GenServer for active entity (room or NPC).
  
  Holds entity state in memory, periodically saves to DB,
  and hibernates after inactivity.
  
  ## Lifecycle
  
  1. Start: Load entity from DB into process state
  2. Active: Handle events, update state, mark dirty
  3. Save: Periodic save of dirty state to DB
  4. Idle: After timeout with no activity, hibernate or stop
  5. Stop: Final save to DB
  """

  use GenServer

  @idle_timeout_ms 300_000      # 5 minutes
  @save_interval_ms 60_000      # 1 minute
  @hibernate_after_ms 120_000   # 2 minutes

  defstruct [
    :entity_id,
    :entity,          # Entity struct
    :dirty,           # true if unsaved changes
    :last_activity,   # DateTime of last interaction
    :save_timer,      # Timer ref for periodic save
    :idle_timer       # Timer ref for idle check
  ]

  # Client API
  def start_link(entity_id, opts \\ [])
  def get(server)
  def get_entity(server)
  def update(server, fun)
  def handle_event(server, event)
  def touch(server)           # Reset idle timer
  def save_now(server)        # Force immediate save
  def stop(server)            # Graceful shutdown

  # GenServer Callbacks
  def init(entity_id)
  def handle_call({:get}, _from, state)
  def handle_call({:update, fun}, _from, state)
  def handle_cast({:event, event}, state)
  def handle_info(:check_idle, state)
  def handle_info(:auto_save, state)
  def terminate(reason, state)
end
```

## State Management

```elixir
defp mark_dirty(state) do
  %{state | dirty: true, last_activity: DateTime.utc_now()}
end

defp save_if_dirty(state) do
  if state.dirty do
    Entities.save_entity(state.entity)
    %{state | dirty: false}
  else
    state
  end
end
```

## Timer Logic

```elixir
def init(entity_id) do
  # Load entity from DB
  entity = Entities.get_entity(entity_id) |> Entities.to_entity()
  
  # Start periodic save timer
  save_timer = Process.send_after(self(), :auto_save, @save_interval_ms)
  
  # Start idle check timer
  idle_timer = Process.send_after(self(), :check_idle, @idle_timeout_ms)
  
  {:ok, %__MODULE__{
    entity_id: entity_id,
    entity: entity,
    dirty: false,
    last_activity: DateTime.utc_now(),
    save_timer: save_timer,
    idle_timer: idle_timer
  }}
end

def handle_info(:check_idle, state) do
  idle_duration = DateTime.diff(DateTime.utc_now(), state.last_activity, :millisecond)
  
  cond do
    idle_duration > @idle_timeout_ms ->
      # Stop process, save state
      {:stop, :normal, save_if_dirty(state)}
      
    idle_duration > @hibernate_after_ms ->
      # Hibernate to reduce memory
      idle_timer = Process.send_after(self(), :check_idle, @idle_timeout_ms)
      {:noreply, %{state | idle_timer: idle_timer}, :hibernate}
      
    true ->

title: Implement Lifecycle Hooks System
description:
Create a hooks system that allows the framework layer to register callbacks for engine lifecycle events.

## Context

Like Evennia's hook methods (`at_object_creation`, `at_pre_cmd`, etc.), we need extension points where the game framework can inject behavior without modifying engine code.

## Current State

- Engine has EventBus for pub/sub
- No hook registration system exists
- Framework code would need to modify engine to add behavior

## Files to Create

### `lib/exmud/engine/hooks.ex`

```elixir
defmodule Exmud.Engine.Hooks do
  @moduledoc """
  Register and execute callbacks for engine lifecycle events.
  
  Hooks provide extension points for the framework layer.
  Unlike events (fire-and-forget), hooks can:
  - Return values that modify behavior
  - Be executed in priority order
  - Halt processing chain
  
  ## Usage
  
      # Register a hook (typically in application startup)
      Hooks.register(:at_entity_creation, MyFramework.Combat, :on_create, priority: 10)
      
      # In engine code, run hooks
      Hooks.run(:at_entity_creation, [entity, context])
      
      # Or run until one returns {:halt, reason}
      case Hooks.run_until_halt(:at_before_move, [entity, destination]) do
        :ok -> proceed_with_move()
        {:halt, reason} -> cancel_move(reason)
      end
  """

  use GenServer

  @hook_types [
    # Entity lifecycle
    :at_entity_creation,
    :at_entity_delete,
    :at_pre_save,
    :at_post_load,

    # Movement
    :at_before_move,
    :at_after_move,
    :at_enter_room,
    :at_leave_room,

    # Perception
    :at_before_look,
    :at_after_look,
    :at_object_receive,
    :at_object_leave,

    # Communication
    :at_before_say,
    :at_after_say,

    # Commands
    :at_pre_command,
    :at_post_command,
    :at_command_fail,

    # Combat (framework can register)
    :at_before_attack,
    :at_after_attack,
    :at_damage,
    :at_death,

    # Scripts
    :at_script_execute,
    :at_script_error
  ]

  # Client API
  def start_link(opts \\ [])
  def register(hook_type, module, function, opts \\ [])
  def unregister(hook_type, module, function)
  def run(hook_type, args)
  def run_until_halt(hook_type, args)
  def list_hooks(hook_type)
  def clear_all()

  # GenServer Implementation
  def init(_opts)
  def handle_call({:register, hook_type, mfa, priority}, _from, state)
  def handle_call({:unregister, hook_type, mfa}, _from, state)
  def handle_call({:run, hook_type, args}, _from, state)
end
```

## Hook Registration

```elixir
# State: %{hook_type => [{priority, {module, function}}]}
def handle_call({:register, hook_type, {module, function}, priority}, _from, state) do
  hooks = Map.get(state, hook_type, [])
  new_hook = {priority, {module, function}}
  updated_hooks = [new_hook | hooks] |> Enum.sort_by(fn {p, _} -> p end)
  {:reply, :ok, Map.put(state, hook_type, updated_hooks)}
end
```

## Hook Execution

```elixir
def run(hook_type, args) do
  hooks = list_hooks(hook_type)
  Enum.each(hooks, fn {_priority, {module, function}} ->
    apply(module, function, args)
  end)
  :ok
end

def run_until_halt(hook_type, args) do
  hooks = list_hooks(hook_type)
  Enum.reduce_while(hooks, :ok, fn {_priority, {module, function}}, _acc ->
    case apply(module, function, args) do
      {:halt, reason} -> {:halt, {:halt, reason}}
      _ -> {:cont, :ok}
    end
  end)
end
```

## Integration Points

Add hook calls to engine core:

```elixir
# In Entities.create_entity/1
def create_entity(attrs) do
  # ... create entity ...
  Hooks.run(:at_entity_creation, [entity, %{}])
  {:ok, entity}
end

# In EntityServer when handling move
def handle_move(state, destination) do
  case Hooks.run_until_halt(:at_before_move, [state.entity, destination]) do
    :ok -> 
      # ... do move ...
      Hooks.run(:at_after_move, [state.entity, old_location, destination])
    {:halt, reason} ->
      {:error, reason}
  end
end
```

## Tests

Create `test/exmud/engine/hooks_test.exs`:
- Register adds hook to list
- Unregister removes hook
- run executes all hooks
- run_until_halt stops on {:halt, reason}
- Priority ordering works
- Invalid hook types are rejected
design: GenServer stores hooks in map by type. Each hook is {priority, {module, function}}. ETS could be used for faster reads if needed. Hooks are sorted by priority on registration.

```elixir
defmodule ExMUD.Framework.Farming.Crop do
  defstruct [
    :key,
    :name,
    :seed_item,
    :growth_stages,      # [{stage, duration, description}]
    :harvest_yield,
    :requires_water,
    :can_wither,
    :wither_time,
    :skill_required,

    :stage_timer,
    :watered,
    :wither_timer
  ]
end
```

## API Functions
- `Farming.list_plots(room)` - Get farm plots in room
- `Farming.can_plant?(entity, room, slot, seed_item)` - Check slot available
- `Farming.plant(entity, room, slot, seed_item)` - Plant seed
- `Farming.water(entity, room, slot)` - Water a crop
- `Farming.harvest(entity, room, slot)` - Harvest ready crop
- `Farming.get_crop_status(room, slot)` - Get stage/description
- `Growth.tick(room)` - Called by game loop for growth progression

## Integration Points
- Inventory for seed consumption and yield
- Skill system for skill bonuses
- Progression for XP rewards
- Weather affects growth (rain = auto-water)

title: Create Example YAML Prototypes for Starter World
description:
Create a set of example YAML prototype files that demonstrate the system and serve as a starter world.

## Context

These files serve multiple purposes:
- Demonstrate YAML format for LLMs and content creators
- Provide a testable starter world
- Act as documentation by example

## Directory Structure to Create

```
priv/world/prototypes/
├── _base/                    # Base prototypes (parents)
│   ├── base_npc.yml
│   ├── base_item.yml
│   ├── base_weapon.yml
│   └── base_room.yml
├── rooms/
│   ├── town_square.yml       # Starting room
│   ├── general_store.yml
│   ├── tavern.yml
│   └── forest_path.yml
├── npcs/
│   ├── merchant.yml
│   ├── tavern_keeper.yml
│   └── goblin.yml
├── items/
│   ├── health_potion.yml
│   ├── rusty_sword.yml
│   └── leather_armor.yml
└── exits/
    └── standard_door.yml
```

## Example Files

### `_base/base_npc.yml`
```yaml
key: base_npc
type: npc
components:
  combatant:
    health:
      current: 50
      max: 50
    stats:
      str: 10
      dex: 10
      sta: 10
    level: 1
tags:
  - npc
```

### `rooms/town_square.yml`
```yaml
key: town_square
type: room
name: "Town Square"
description: |
  You stand in the heart of a small village. A weathered stone 
  fountain bubbles in the center, surrounded by cobblestones worn 
  smooth by countless feet. Buildings cluster around the square:
  a general store to the north, and a lively tavern to the east.
exits:
  north: general_store
  east: tavern
  south: forest_path
spawns:
  - prototype: merchant
    count: 1
tags:
  - town
  - safe_zone
  - starting_area
```

### `npcs/merchant.yml`
```yaml
key: merchant
parent: base_npc
type: npc
name: "Grizzled Merchant"
description: |
  A weathered trader with keen eyes watches over his wares.
  Years of haggling have sharpened his wit and loosened his tongue.
components:
  combatant:
    health:
      current: 100
      max: 100
  conversant:
    dialogue_tree:
      start:
        text: "Welcome, traveler! Looking to buy or sell?"
        choices:
          - label: "Show me your wares"
            next: show_wares
          - label: "What news from the road?"
            next: rumors
          - label: "Farewell"
            next: goodbye
      show_wares:
        text: "I've got potions, weapons, and armor. What interests you?"
        choices:
          - label: "Back"
            next: start
      rumors:
        text: "They say goblins have been spotted in the forest to the south..."
        choices:
          - label: "Tell me more"
            next: goblin_quest
          - label: "Back"
            next: start
      goblin_quest:
        text: "Clear them out and I'll reward you handsomely."
        choices:
          - label: "I'll do it"
            action: offer_quest
            quest_id: clear_goblins
          - label: "Maybe later"
            next: start
      goodbye:
        text: "Safe travels!"
        end: true
tags:
  - friendly
  - quest_giver
  - merchant
attributes:
  shop_inventory:
    - health_potion
    - rusty_sword
    - leather_armor
```

## Implementation Notes

- Use consistent formatting (2-space indent, quoted strings for names)
- Multi-line descriptions use YAML block scalar `|`
- All prototypes should be valid against Prototype struct
- Cross-references (exits, spawns) use prototype keys

## Validation

After creating files, run:
```elixir
Exmud.Engine.PrototypeLoader.load_all()
Exmud.Engine.PrototypeLoader.validate_all()
```
